steps.say: This is the commonest surgical cause of newborn bowel blockage, and boys dominate the ward. Hirschsprung disease affects 1 in 5000 births with fourfold male excess, and 3 to 5 percent carry Down syndrome. The RET oncogene on chromosome 10 explains the familial cases.
steps.tx: **Hirschsprung disease** (congenital colonic blockage) is distal **aganglionosis** (missing nerve ganglia) of myenteric and submucosal plexuses in 1 in **5000** births with **4** fold male excess, **3** to **5** percent with Down syndrome, and **RET oncogene** (chromosome **10** signal gene) in familial cases.

steps.say: The last stretch of bowel cannot relax, so milk piles up behind a normally built colon. Failed relaxation of the distal colon and internal sphincter creates functional obstruction where the narrow distal segment is abnormal and the dilated proximal bowel is normal. Peristalsis waves crash against the closed segment.
steps.tx: Failed relaxation of the distal colon and **internal sphincter** (anal muscle ring) creates **functional obstruction** (blockage without a lump) where the narrow distal segment is abnormal and the dilated proximal bowel is normal. **Peristalsis** (propulsive waves) cannot cross the aganglionic segment.

vis.alt: Colon diagram showing slow transit with impacted hard stool beside rectal section with puborectalis sling and acute anorectal angle.
vis.caption: Failed relaxation creates functional obstruction with impaction behind a narrow distal segment. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Disease always starts at the anus and creeps upward, so length determines the operation. Aganglionosis starts at the anorectal line with transition to normal colon in rectosigmoid in 80 percent, splenic or transverse colon in 17 percent, and total colonic aganglionosis with small bowel in 8 percent.
steps.tx: Aganglionosis starts at the anorectal line with **transition zone** (changeover funnel) to normal colon in **rectosigmoid** (rectum and sigmoid) in **80** percent, splenic or transverse colon in **17** percent, and **total colonic aganglionosis** (whole colon plus small bowel) in **8** percent.

steps.say: Most cases are declaring themselves in the nursery with a swollen belly and green vomit. Over 90 percent present as newborns with abdominal distention and bilious vomiting plus delayed meconium beyond 24 hours. Enterocolitis with diarrhea, fever, hematochezia, shock and death remains the leading killer.
steps.tx: Over **90** percent present as newborns with **abdominal distention** (swollen belly) and bilious vomiting plus **delayed meconium** (no stool in **24** hours), while missed cases return with chronic constipation. **Enterocolitis** (infected dilated colon with diarrhea, fever and shock) is the leading killer.

steps.say: The enema film shows a thin distal pipe opening into a huge loaded colon, a picture worth memorising. Contrast enema shows a narrow distal rectum with transition zone and dilated proximal sigmoid, and contrast retention at 24 hours strongly indicates disease. The same study excludes plug, small left colon and atresia.
steps.tx: **Contrast enema** (dye study) shows a narrow distal rectum with transition zone and dilated proximal sigmoid, and **contrast retention** (dye still present) at **24** hours strongly indicates disease. The study also excludes meconium plug, small left colon and colonic atresia mimics.

nodes.label: Retention at 24 hours confirms; biopsy follows

steps.say: Only tissue settles the diagnosis, because scans can mislead in small babies. Suction rectal biopsy proximal to the dentate line is the gold standard, needing specimens 5 millimetres to 1 centimetre above it and two samples 1 centimetre apart posteriorly in infants. Absent ganglia with hypertrophied trunks, acetylcholinesterase staining and calretinin confirm disease.
steps.tx: Suction **rectal biopsy** (mucosal sample) proximal to the **dentate line** (anal canal landmark) is the gold standard, needing specimens **5** mm to **1** cm above it and two samples **1** cm apart posteriorly in infants. Absent ganglia, hypertrophied trunks, acetylcholinesterase staining and **calretinin** (nerve marker) confirm it.

steps.say: Three classic operations all give similar function once ganglionated bowel is pulled down. Swenson full thickness dissection, Soave endorectal dissection with posterior cuff myotomy usually laparoscopic assisted and transanal, and Duhamel retrorectal pull with side to side neorectum give similar function after frozen section confirmed ganglionated pull through.
steps.tx: **Swenson** (1949 full thickness dissection), **Soave** (endorectal dissection with posterior cuff myotomy, usually laparoscopic assisted and transanal), and **Duhamel** (retrorectal pull with side to side neorectum) give similar function after frozen section confirmed ganglionated pull through. Intraoperative frozen section confirms ganglion cells before any anastomosis is constructed.

steps.say: Most babies undergo one stage pull through after washouts clear the loaded colon. Irrigations with a soft red rubber catheter and saline clear effluent first, with leveling colostomy reserved for failed irrigation or long segment disease. Follow up controls postoperative constipation and soiling, with rebiopsy for transition zone at the anastomosis.
steps.tx: Most undergo one stage pull through after **rectal irrigations** (saline washouts) with a soft red rubber catheter and saline clear effluent, with **leveling colostomy** (venting stoma) reserved for failed irrigation or long segment disease. Follow up controls **postoperative constipation** (lingering dysmotility) and soiling.
